💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending big money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge.
  • Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID.
  • Industry observers note that that remarked, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending big money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge. The latest showpiece is the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, a one-off electric hatchback built for the track that sheds a set of doors and borrows the electric motor from its bigger brothers.

Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID. Polo GTI and the upcoming ID.3 GTI, and its purpose is to show what the German brand can do with its modular MEB+ platform. In fact, Volkswagen is calling itself the “master of modular platforms,” proudly saying that the same architecture that underpins the bog-standard ID. Polo is capable of impressive extremes, from the ultra-efficient Mission Efficiency to the performance-oriented GTI Clubsport EV.

Industry observers note that that remarked, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy. Engineers had to take an APP550 electric motor, which was originally designed for rear-wheel-drive models like the ID.7 and ID. Tiguan, and adapt it for the ID. Polo chassis, which is front-wheel-drive.

To fit the larger drive unit in the small hatchback, the whole front section of the car had to be modified, which meant designing and building an entirely new subframe. The longitudinal chassis members, stabilizer bar, several mounting points, and various chassis components also had to be redesigned to make the taller APP550 drive unit fit under the hood.

In a recent development, what’s more, the high-voltage charger, air conditioning compressor, thermal management module, and the water pump had to be relocated. Designers and engineers worked together to develop special holders, adapters, and mounting concepts to make it all work.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept’s powertrain makes 362 horsepower and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton-meters) of torque, making it the most powerful electric Polo ever made. Compared to the road-going ID. Polo GTI, it makes 139 more horsepower and 192 more pound-feet of torque.

Yet, the car is still front-wheel drive. And if you’ve driven a relatively torquey EV with FWD, you know that transferring everything that an electric drive unit can give to the front wheels can prove difficult. But Volkswagen has that covered with an electronic front differential lock that uses a multiplate clutch. With it, the car can transfer power to both wheels if one of them starts to lose traction.

All of that power and torque give the electric track car a zero-to-62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) sprint time of 4.7 seconds and a 149 miles pr hour (240 kilometers per hour) top speed. To enable this level of performance, the 52-kilowatt-hour battery, which is the same as in the production ID. Polo GTI, was tweaked to allow for a higher power output of up to 290 kW, as well as longer discharge periods at high outputs.

Industry observers note that hooked to a DC fast charger, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can take up to 105 kW, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI, which can go from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.

Industry observers note that the extra power and torque go hand in hand with plenty of changes to the body and underneath it. The one-off EV is 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) wider than the production model and sits 30 mm (1.1 in) lower than the standard ID. Polo. The same adaptive suspension as the production vehicle is used, but its setup is adjusted for track use.

Sources indicate that the electric Clubsport Concept has just two doors instead of the regular ID. Polo’s four, and features a pretty aggressive body kit with wide wheel arches, functional air ducts, and a huge rear wing. GTI badges and red accents are everywhere, including in the interior, where the central touchscreen no longer acts as the infotainment center. In fact, the concept doesn’t have an infotainment system, as the central screen handles driving settings exclusively.

Bright red five-point harnesses protect the driver and front passenger sitting in Recaro racing bucket seats, while a red rollover bar has replaced the rear seats and cargo area.

The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is not yet intended for production, but the German automaker hasn’t ruled out the option entirely, saying that it has always associated the development of concept vehicles “with the theoretical option of turning a one-off into a fresh production derivative.”.

The track-focused EV will make its first live appearance at the Essen Motor Show in Germany, which runs from November 27 through December 6.

The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 Remake

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?).
  • Recent findings suggest that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game.
  • In a recent development, for the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?). Now in its second remake, not every secret has made its way forward through the previous iterations, but many have. Below you will learn about a few of the secrets that made the cut, and others that didn’t.

Recent findings suggest that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game. If you don’t rush to Zelda and instead pause and enter first-person to look around, you will see portraits of other Nintendo characters through the windows, like Mario and Yoshi. In the 3DS remake, the portraits are replaced by an image of a Mario stage.

In a recent development, for the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters. Instead, the tapestry you build over the course of the game is on display. Removing the reference to Nintendo characters outside of the Zelda universe is understandable, but it is a little odd that art representing the full adventure of the game – an adventure that has not yet concluded – is on the wall.

It has been revealed that as stated above, the Nintendo character portraits are gone, but there is still a guard you can annoy. If you fire a Deku Seed into the left window, a guard will pop out, yell at you, and then throw a bomb at you. You can’t pick up the bomb. In fact, at this point in the game, you haven’t even seen a bomb.

Sources indicate that the Hyrule Castle portrait references to Yoshi and Mario are gone (though Mario and Luigi are still kind of in the game in a way), but Bowser gets a pass for some reason. Both Malon and her dad, Talon, are still wearing Bowser pins on their clothes. And unlike the N64 game where the detail was a little vague, there is no mistaking it here.

Gossip Stones are all over Ocarina of Time and it takes a while to understand what they do. If you hit them with a sword, they tell you the time, and if you play Zelda’s Lullaby near them, they refill your magic. If you do the Happy Mask Salesman’s side quest, interacting with them while wearing the Mask of Truth offers little hints and details about the world. But then there are interactions that are just odd for no reason. Blowing up a bomb near a Gossip Stone still makes it take off like a rocket ship, and using the Megaton Hammer still flattens them for a moment like a Looney Tunes.

And speaking of playing Zelda’s Lullaby for inanimate objects, if you slash a sign to pieces with your sword and regret your words and deeds, you can play the iconic tune to make the signs reform and become readable again.

This detail was exclusive to the 3DS remake of Ocarina of Time, and surprising no one, it has been removed. Ocarina of Time launched in June 2011 and Nintendo released Skyward Sword about five months later in November. For… marketing purposes, I guess, Skyward Sword art could be found in Lonlon Ranch, the Bombchu Shop in Hyrule Castle Town, and the Gerudo Fortress. It was a fun Easter Egg to discover back in 2011, especially since Skyward Sword was still months away, but these days it’s a bit of an odd inclusion.

It has been revealed that though never explicit, the composer ghosts guarding the Sun’s Song (and Link’s first ReDead encounter) have always been assumed to be inspired by Mario and Luigi. They are brothers; Flat is short, squat, and red; Sharp is lanky and green. They still appear in Ocarina of Time this way, which isn't surprising, since they are important characters you must meet to get a very useful song. Fans have also speculated that Talon and Ingo are Mario and Luigi-inspired for similar reasons, but it’s worth noting that they are not brothers.

In the Spirit Temple there is a large statue of a woman and for reasons that have never been explained, Link could attach his hookshot to her breasts. It served no purpose. It didn’t help solve a puzzle. If anything, it was confusing. But we all tried it and there is no shame in admitting it! That was removed for the 3DS remake, and it remains removed in 2026.

This is a very subtle reference to Wind Waker/Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom and is potentially the only addition to the remake that looks toward the future of the Zelda franchise. Obviously, plenty of characters in Ocarina later appear in Majora’s Mask (another remake of that is hopefully being considered), but it would be inaccurate to call those intentional Easter Eggs.

Recent findings suggest that however, in Kokiri Forest and in the neighboring Lost Woods, the magical debris floating in the air often resembles a Korok as it would later appear in the series. It makes sense, too, because the Koroks are meant to be what the Kokiri transformed into following The Great Flood.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

It has been revealed that bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

Industry observers note that the 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a company that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

Industry observers note that getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

All in all, it looks really badass and shows that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the upcoming Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s significant investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

It has been revealed that you’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6.
  • This wasn't simply an overlooked feature.
  • It has been revealed that in its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6. One old activity, though, isn't making the cut. Players can no longer hire sex workers, ending a feature that's been part of the series since Grand Theft Auto 3 arrived in 2001.

This wasn't simply an overlooked feature. Rockstar deliberately left it out. Shacknews asked the GTA studio about it, and they confirmed the feature was removed. Rockstar also offered an explanation, and it comes down to the kind of story it wants to tell with Jason and Lucia.

It has been revealed that in its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run. The studio remarked it had considered which familiar GTA elements would work alongside the characters and the relationship at the center of the game, rather than bringing back every previous feature by default.

In a recent development, rockstar pointed to systems such as police pursuits, radio stations, robberies, and car theft as examples of the elements it carried forward. Those all fit the criminal adventures Jason and Lucia get caught up in. Hiring sex workers, apparently, didn't fit what the team had in mind.

Industry observers note that it's an interesting explanation because Rockstar didn't claim the removal was due to a technical limitation or a ratings requirement. Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

It has been revealed that anyone who's watched the GTA 6 launch trailer will have seen how much of the marketing revolves around the pair. Rockstar keeps bringing the focus back to Jason and Lucia, even when the trailers show off everything else happening in Leonida. Their story is the reason the two playable protagonists are together in the first place.

Sources indicate that hiring sex workers first became a recognizable open-world interaction in GTA 3, and it remained available across later mainline games, including Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5. For some players, it became one of those strange little things they expected to find when wandering around a GTA city at night.

It also brings back one of GTA 3's more infamous controversies. Players could hire a sex worker, kill her afterward, and pick up the money they'd just spent. That drew plenty of criticism at the time, and the mechanic stuck around. It was still possible in GTA 5.

Sources indicate that I can't help connecting this to Jason Schreier's 2022 Bloomberg report, which noted Rockstar was trying to avoid jokes that punch down at marginalized groups. He suggested GTA 6 might feel quite different from GTA 5, and seeing this particular feature disappear makes me think he might have been onto something. Rockstar claims it's about Jason and Lucia, of course, but I wonder if both things played a part.

Recent findings suggest that it was never the reason most people played these games, of course. But GTA has always made a point of filling its streets with activities that aren't strictly necessary for completing missions. The series' reputation comes as much from those distractions as it does from car chases, shootouts, and elaborate heists.

In a recent development, that's why removing a relatively minor interaction is still newsworthy. It has survived several generations of GTA, across different protagonists and settings. Now that Rockstar is putting two characters in a relationship at the heart of its newest game, that particular carryover has finally been dropped.

It has been revealed that this doesn't mean GTA 6 has suddenly become a tame version of Grand Theft Auto. The game's nightlife is very much present. Our guide to GTA 6's strip clubs already covers several venues around Leonida, so the absence of one activity shouldn't be confused with the removal of adult entertainment altogether.

There's a distinction between the atmosphere of Vice City and the specific actions Rockstar lets the protagonists take. A setting can still have strip clubs and the more outrageous side of GTA without including every interaction that existed in previous games.

The confirmation is also about a specific action players can take. It doesn't establish whether sex workers appear in the game as background characters, or whether the story mentions them. Rockstar answered a question about the gameplay interaction, not every possible appearance of the subject.

Some fans will probably find the change strange, particularly if they've been playing since the PS2 days. Others might not have noticed the feature was missing at all. Either way, it's one of the clearer examples of Rockstar choosing to leave an old mechanic behind instead of carrying it over simply because it's always been there.

In a recent development, for a series known for giving players countless ways to get distracted, that's a notable decision. And this time, at least, Rockstar has given a pretty straightforward reason for making it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.

In a recent development, first, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The company then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this new trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.

According to recent reports, the GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.

Industry observers note that like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t announced pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

The Switch 2 Pro Controller Can Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Even Better

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent.
  • According to recent reports, after hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint.
  • If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the new free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the new Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I promptly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

According to recent reports, after hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the new free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

In a recent development, if you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

Recent findings suggest that and the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is newly introduced for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

In a recent development, even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

The Remnants Of The Electric Saab That Never Was Are Going Up For Auction

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer.
  • In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.
  • In a recent development, the entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer. Maybe it’s because it was always a little left-field, even when it was part of General Motors, or maybe I liked the cars’ design.

In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.

In a recent development, the entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik. The lot includes a working mule prototype, bodies, parts, accessories, drawings, and four complete Emily GT prototypes, which are billed as the only ones that will ever be available on the open market.

Developed by ex-Saab engineers who worked at NEVS, the firm that picked up the pieces after the storied automaker’s bankruptcy in 2012, the Emily GT was envisioned as a next-generation electric model with four in-wheel motors and a driving range of up to 600 miles, courtesy of a high-voltage battery that could, in theory, top out at 175 kilowatt-hours. According to technical drawings obtained by SaabPlanet, the standard-range car would have had a 105-kWh pack, while the mid-spec model was designed for a 140-kWh pack.

Wireless charging at up to 11 kW was also in the cards, and no fewer than four body styles, including a shooting brake, a sporty sedan, a two-door coupe, and a cabriolet.

The four electric motors, developing a combined 490 horsepower, enabled a quite sophisticated torque vectoring system, leading to great road manners. However, none of it materialized. NEVS never had the cash to move forward with the project, and now all of the pieces are being sold off.

“For us, this is a historic event, and I believe many Saab fans feel the same way,” mentioned Nina Selander, CEO of NEVS. “Despite only ever being built as a handful of prototypes, the Emily GT has achieved iconic status. That states a lot about the fascination with the car. By making the sale available in this way, we hope to attract car enthusiasts all over the world whose hearts beat for Saab.”.

For the right buyer, it’s the perfect starter kit for a new car company, but it won’t come cheap. According to the Swedish local newspaper Ttela, the starting bid will be roughly $1.5 million (15 million SEK), and the auction house is not splitting the lot’s components into individual pieces. Everything is bundled into a single lot, so whoever has the highest bid goes home with everything.

Separately, Klaravik is auctioning off the world’s only NEVS Sango, a prototype of a self-driving vehicle designed for public transport that never materialized.

Both online auctions will go live on November 25 and will run through December 9.

The 12 Best-Looking Newly introduced Cars on the Market in 2027

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the average car has about 30,000 pieces, if you count individual nuts and bolts.
  • Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.
  • Nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the average car has about 30,000 pieces, if you count individual nuts and bolts. It’s difficult enough to put all of that together, but it’s even more difficult to make it look good. While there are plenty of decent-looking upcoming cars on the market, the ones that go above and beyond in the design department truly shimmer. You’ll notice that our preferences trend towards sports cars, but we’ve also included plenty of sedans, a single SUV, and a wide range of price points. Among the plethora of vehicles that have cycled through our office, here are our picks for the best-looking cars on the market today.

Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.

Nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup. It looks fantastic as both a coupe and as a convertible. The active rear spoiler manages to maintain the sports car’s sleek profile whether it’s engaged or not, and the low nose with a thin, sweeping grille is classic Ferrari. The 296 drives as good as it looks, too, thanks to its hybrid powertrain that uses a twin-turbo V-6 engine.

In a recent development, the Miata has been an enthusiast staple since it entered the market wide-eyed and grinning in 1990. Since then, it’s grown up a bit, replacing pop-up headlights with angular, cat-like eyes and turning the grin into a bit more of a snarl. It’s a head-turner in any generation, but the newest ND is the sportiest model yet, and it’s best enjoyed with the top down. We also love the look of the Retractable Fastback (RF) body style pictured here. For an incredibly fun and affordable sports car, the Miata is truly always the answer.

More About the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

Recent findings suggest that while the Genesis brand isn’t quite as well-established as Mercedes or BMW, its flagship G90 looks every bit the part of a luxury sedan. Thin, sweeping taillights punctuate the nicely shaped rear end, while the classic diamond-shaped grille integrates beautifully with the slim, low-profile headlights. The G90 looks, sounds, and feels silky, and its sub-$100,000 starting price tag is surprising given how special it is.

Like the G90, the GV70’s sophisticated design language helps it punch above its weight against the Porsches and Mercedes-Benzes in its segment. The GV70’s sporty body lines and interior details, including a knurled glass shift knob, make it feel like a true luxury vehicle. Genesis added a Prestige Graphite trim to the lineup for 2027, which makes the GV70 look even sportier with carbon-fiber pieces, darkened trim, and red brake calipers.

When Maserati brought back the GranTurismo nameplate in 2024, the sports car got a subtle redesign that brought out all of the best qualities found in the previous generation. Since then, it’s only gotten better thanks to a styling refresh for 2027. With a cheerfully aggressive front end and a sloped, sleek rear that tapers nicely, the GranTurismo coupe exudes high-performance fun in a stylish two-door package.

More About the Maserati GranTurismo.

The Lotus Emira looks great from any angle, and its gorgeously proportioned styling rivals much more expensive exotics. The Emira is a true stripped-back sports car, with just the necessities inside the cabin and a heavy focus on performance and agility. It’s unmistakably a mid-engined car, as the rear fenders flare out to make room for the hefty air intakes behind the doors, and the sleek roofline melts seamlessly into an angular rear end for a spunky-yet-elegant silhouette.

Lucid recently took pole position in our top-ranked car brands list, and both the Air and the Gravity SUV have won our 10Best award in the past. Beyond its stunning performance, the Lucid Air’s styling promotes a sense of practical luxury that looks upscale without shouting about it. Modern-looking light signatures at the front and rear lean into minimalistic design trends, and the sedan’s interior looks just as stealthy as its exterior.

The muscular Vantage is full of British charm as either a coupe or as a roadster. Its long-hood, short-deck proportions perfectly complement the twin-turbo V-8 under the hood, and the cabin looks tastefully upscale. The detailing is exquisite, too. There’s a reason James Bond’s car of choice is so often an Aston Martin.

More About the Aston Martin Vantage.

Sources indicate that the current Nissan Z brings the gorgeous 240Z of the past into the modern day while preserving much of its original characteristics. There’s also a hint of the 300ZX in its taillight shape. For 2027, the Z got a slight makeover, which makes the front grille a bit slimmer than its boxy predecessor and refines a few body lines at the rear. The Z perfectly toes the line between nostalgia and future-focused styling.

The two-door CLE-class takes everything great about the C-class and E-class sedans and packages those characteristics into a far more sophisticated-looking coupe. From the side, the CLE looks long and slender, and the nicely shaped headlights and taillights further cement the car’s sleek proportions. The long hood gives off a hint of AMG GT proportions for about $50K less, and if you seek a more aggressive appearance, the AMG CLE53 version amps up the look with a wide-body stance and other tweaks.

More About the Mercedes-Benz CLE-Class.

Industry observers note that though it’s been around for a long time now, the Giulia remains an enjoyable sports sedan, and its exterior styling flaunts its unique Italian flair in a class dominated by German brands. Alfa’s classic three-part grille dominates the front end without being gaudy, and the signature teledial wheels are a focal point along the sides. Giulias are a bit of a rarity in the United States, so they’re instant eye-catchers on American roads.

More About the Alfa Romeo Giulia.

It has been revealed that the Lexus LC was discontinued after the 2026 model year, but it looks so good that we included it anyway. As both a coupe and a convertible, the LC rocks a striking yet refined look that’s worth every penny of its six-figure price tag. The LC looks like nothing else on the road, and its wedge shape with many sharp angles still feels like a concept car for the street. Lexus offers plenty of unique interior color schemes, too, which are just as important as the exterior when you want to put the top down and show off a bit.

Industry observers note that alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports has revealed 3 latest Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

Industry observers note that the Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

Latest Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.
  • We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the new GTI hot hatch earlier this week.
  • Volkswagen launched the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the new GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

Volkswagen launched the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a latest era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, mentioned.

After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

It has been revealed that the fresh ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept indicates “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

It’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

Sources indicate that the Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, said the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”.

Sources indicate that thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen noted, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added fresh ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

Industry observers note that the Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

Recent findings suggest that on the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a upcoming diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

According to recent reports, inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Sources indicate that following the ID. Polo GTI, newly introduced ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

Sources indicate that the company will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm looks to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

The standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.

That's exactly what happened to content creator JasonTheWeen, who had a particularly rough launch day after making one unfortunate mistake with his PlayStation 5.

Sources indicate that with around 1.3 million followers on YouTube, the content creator had been streaming an extended session of Rockstar's latest adventure. However, after accidentally turning off his console, he returned to the game only to find that his entire 11-hour save was missing!

According to The Economic Times, he later explained that his foot had accidentally hit the switch on an extension cord, cutting power to his PS5. The moment he realized what had happened was captured live, and his reaction was understandably heartbreaking. Here, take a look:.

Recent findings suggest that visibly devastated, the streamer struggled to hold back tears and repeatedly shouted about the 11 hours he had just lost. He then contacted someone from his team to ask whether there was any way to recover his progress, even if that meant getting back to the beginning of the second chapter rather than having to start the entire adventure again.

Unfortunately, it seems that it wasn’t possible, and he eventually brought a friend to help him rush through the sections he had already completed, hoping to get his marathon back on track.

Industry observers note that the exact reason behind the incident remains unclear, but there's a possible explanation involving the game's save system. GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain vital events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

One possibility is that JasonTheWeen accidentally turned off his PS5 while the game was writing save data. If that happened, interrupting the process could have corrupted the save file, potentially explaining why so much progress disappeared when he rolled out the game again.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain important events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

In a recent development, it's important to stress that this is only a theory, and neither Rockstar nor the streamer has confirmed what actually caused the loss. We also don't know whether the save can be recovered, so it would be unfair to draw conclusions about the game's autosave system based on this single incident.

Still, the situation is a good reminder that manually saving your progress is worth the extra few seconds. GTA 6 offers multiple manual save slots, allowing players to keep separate backups instead of relying exclusively on autosaving. This can be particularly useful after completing a long mission or spending hours exploring Leonida.

For anyone planning to sink an entire afternoon into the game, taking a moment to create a manual save might save you from a very unpleasant surprise later!

Unfortunately, losing his progress wasn't the only upsetting moment JasonTheWeen experienced during the stream. Shortly afterward, he heard shouting outside his home and informed viewers that police officers had arrived at his property.

Sources indicate that the incident appears to have been a case of swatting, a dangerous prank involving false emergency reports intended to send police officers to someone's home. It's an especially unpleasant situation for any streamer, and it made an already frustrating day considerably worse.

Following the incident, JasonTheWeen also reached out to Rockstar and Sony on social media, asking whether his lost progress could be recovered. For now, there's no confirmed response from either organization about his request or why all the progress was lost.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

Industry observers note that before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

In a recent development, ocarina of Time is easily one of the most important video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

According to recent reports, are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

And my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

According to recent reports, and then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

According to recent reports, you mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

#63725. Tech Report: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event

Tech Report: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that NASA scientists are tracking an exceptionally powerful El Niño that could grow even larger than the historic 1997 event, which brought extreme weather to regions around the world.
  • Recent findings suggest that el Niño is a recurring climate phenomenon that typically develops every two to seven years, when ocean temperatures rise above normal across parts of the equatorial Pacific.
  • It has been revealed that two of the most powerful recent El Niño events occurred in 1997-98 and 2015-16.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that NASA scientists are tracking an exceptionally powerful El Niño that could grow even larger than the historic 1997 event, which brought extreme weather to regions around the world. Using 35 years of satellite observations, researchers can now compare the rapidly developing 2026 El Niño with some of the strongest events ever recorded, revealing remarkable similarities and crucial differences.

Recent findings suggest that el Niño is a recurring climate phenomenon that typically develops every two to seven years, when ocean temperatures rise above normal across parts of the equatorial Pacific. These changes can disrupt atmospheric circulation and alter weather patterns far beyond the Pacific Ocean.

It has been revealed that two of the most powerful recent El Niño events occurred in 1997-98 and 2015-16. Both had widespread consequences, including destructive fires in Indonesia and the Amazon, severe drought and crop failures in southern Africa, and intense rainfall and coastal flooding in Southern California. Now, the 2026 El Niño is emerging as another major event, with satellite data suggesting it could rival those historic episodes.

How El Niño Builds Strength in the Pacific.

The development of El Niño depends on a complex interaction between ocean temperatures and atmospheric winds.

Under normal conditions, steady trade winds push warm surface water toward the western Pacific Ocean. This causes warm water to accumulate in the west, where the ocean surface sits slightly higher than it does farther east.

According to recent reports, when the trade winds weaken, some of that warm water begins moving eastward across the Pacific. The shift can weaken the winds even further or occasionally cause them to reverse direction. This allows additional warm water to spread east, reinforcing the process and raising ocean temperatures and sea levels across the central and eastern Pacific.

Industry observers note that although the underlying process is similar each time, no two El Niño events develop in exactly the same way. Their behavior depends partly on where the warmest water accumulates and how the atmosphere responds to the changing ocean conditions.

Sources indicate that "The search for the 'typical' El Niño is very elusive," said Josh Willis, project scientist for sea level missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). "They're all different in terms of where they land and how their impacts play out.".

NASA Satellites Reveal Striking Similarities to 1997.

To understand how the current El Niño compares with earlier events, scientists are examining decades of satellite measurements of ocean surface height.

This technique, called satellite altimetry, measures subtle changes in the elevation of the ocean surface. Because seawater expands as it becomes warmer, unusually high sea levels in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific can reveal where heat is accumulating during El Niño.

According to recent reports, NASA's comparison maps show differences in Pacific Ocean surface height on October 13, 1997 (left), and October 12, 2026 (right). The earlier measurements were collected by the TOPEX/Poseidon satellite, while the newer observations came from the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite. Scientists at JPL processed both datasets to make the events easier to compare.

According to recent reports, the maps use red to identify areas where the ocean surface is higher than its usual level, while white represents normal conditions and blue reveals areas where sea levels are below average. To better isolate the effects of El Niño and other temporary natural changes, researchers removed variations associated with seasonal patterns and long-term trends.

In a recent development, one major advantage of these observations is their remarkable consistency. Successive satellite missions have followed nearly identical paths, with overlapping periods of operation that allow scientists to compare measurements across decades.

"What's unique about altimetry is that we have a 35-year record from nearly identical satellites flying almost the same ground track, with each mission overlapping the next," Willis said. "That lets us look back in time and compare this El Niño to what happened in 1997. And right now, this one is on track to be even bigger.".

Why the 2026 El Niño Resembles a Historic Climate Giant.

Recent findings suggest that the 2026 El Niño intensified much more abruptly than the powerful 1997-98 event. Despite that difference in timing, NASA's satellite measurements from October reveal striking similarities in how the two events are developing.

Industry observers note that in both cases, the Pacific displays a pronounced difference in sea level (low in the west and high in the east). The observations also show elevated, unusually warm water stretching eastward along the equator until it reaches the coast of South America.

It has been revealed that these similarities suggest that the 2026 event could produce weather effects resembling those experienced during the 1997-98 El Niño. That earlier episode brought substantial rainfall to California and other parts of the southern United States, raising the possibility of comparable conditions during the coming winter.

However, the powerful 2015-16 El Niño demonstrates why similarities in overall strength do not necessarily translate into identical weather impacts.

For that comparison, NASA scientists also examined ocean surface height measurements from October 12, 2015, recorded by the Jason-2 satellite. The data were placed alongside observations from approximately the same time of year in 1997 and 2026.

Although the 2015 event also featured exceptionally warm water and elevated sea levels along the equator, that warm water did not extend toward the South American coast as strongly as it did during the other two events.

According to recent reports, the resulting rainfall patterns were different as well. During the winter of 2015-16, much of the precipitation associated with El Niño was concentrated over Central America and the southeastern United States, while Mexico experienced significant flooding.

Will El Niño Bring Extreme Weather in Winter 2026-27?

The latest observations have prompted scientists to closely monitor how the 2026 El Niño develops and what it could mean for weather conditions in the months ahead.

In its October 8, 2026, outlook, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) estimated an 83 percent chance that strong to very strong El Niño conditions would occur during the first three months of 2027.

That forecast points to the potential for a particularly significant climate event, but it does not establish exactly where the most severe effects will occur.

Industry observers note that el Niño can influence weather across much of the planet by changing the movement of heat and moisture through the atmosphere. However, those effects become increasingly difficult to predict farther from the tropical Pacific, where other atmospheric processes can alter or weaken the expected patterns.

As a result, even the strong resemblance between the 2026 and 1997 events cannot guarantee that the coming winter will unfold in the same way.

"There's always a bit of a dice roll here," Willis said. "Just because this El Niño looks like 1997 doesn't mean it will be exactly the same -- it's just our best guess at the moment.".

In a recent development, the unprecedented consistency of the satellite record gives researchers a valuable way to recognize familiar patterns and evaluate the scale of the developing El Niño. But whether 2026-27 ultimately matches the extreme weather of previous historic events will depend on how the ocean and atmosphere interact in the months ahead.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe.
  • According to recent reports, it also didn’t wait for Brussels.
  • In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini declared the decision on X on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe. Italy becomes the 12th European country to allow the system, and the first of the EU’s significant markets.

According to recent reports, it also didn’t wait for Brussels. The EU committee that decides on bloc-wide recognition isn’t expected to vote until December at the earliest.

In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini declared the decision on X on Friday. He wrote that the ministry (MIT) gave the green light after a “thorough technical feasibility check,” and that Italy is getting ahead of the EU recognition process, which he described as “still being defined.”.

Industry observers note that tesla Europe followed with a one-liner, “Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon,” and a video of one of its cars driving itself through Rome. There’s no firm rollout date yet.

It’s still a Level 2 driver-assist system. It can steer, brake, accelerate, and handle intersections and lane changes, but the driver has to supervise at all times and stays fully responsible for the car.

In a recent development, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW was first, approving FSD Supervised on April 10 under Article 39 of the EU type-approval regulation. Other member states can then recognize that approval nationally, one by one.

Ten did before Italy: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Those are mostly small markets. Together with the Netherlands, they add up to about 70 million people, or roughly 15% of the EU’s population.

Italy alone has about 59 million people, so Friday’s decision nearly doubles the share of Europeans who can legally use the system, to close to 30%.

According to recent reports, rome’s position moved fast. In April, Senator Carlo Calenda formally asked Salvini’s ministry to prioritize the approval. On October 29, Salvini posted that he’d had a “very positive and constructive” call with Elon Musk and that Italy supported a “swift EU approval,” which read at the time as backing for an EU-level decision, not a national one. Three weeks later, Italy went national.

Industry observers note that A lot changed in between. Tesla dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe after Germany’s Transport Ministry called it misleading, and cut the maximum speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit. Then on November 16, the RDW approved stricter driver monitoring, including hands on the wheel above 130 km/h. That’s the version Italy is approving.

According to recent reports, the EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) pushed the Tesla vote to December after holding only discussions in October. Bloc-wide approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU population.

According to recent reports, germany said in October it would back approval after Tesla agreed to the rename and the speed cap. If it follows through, Germany and the 12 approving countries would cover roughly 47% of the EU’s population.

That’s progress for Tesla, but it’s not 65%. France refused a national approval in July, and Spain hasn’t recognized the Dutch approval. Tesla needs at least one of them, plus most of the remaining holdouts.

It has been revealed that if Tesla makes enough changes to FSD, they will get approval. Once you have a major market like Italy sign on, then its only a matter of time before FSD is approved everywhere else. What I am interested in seeing is how FSD is utilized by European drivers and how any concerns are presented and addressed as there most certainly will be.

This is a real win for Tesla, and for Italian owners with HW4 cars who have been paying for a feature they couldn’t use at home. Italy is Tesla’s first significant European market to say yes, and it shifts momentum going into December.

But it’s pretty crazy that now Europe is going to get a safer FSD than in the US.

I bet that this will get reflected in the data, if we ever get to see it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

It has been revealed that the Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Industry observers note that pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

Interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

In a recent development, if you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

BYD's Latest SUV Can Hide Its Steering Wheel When You Don't Need It

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI.
  • The Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range.
  • Power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI. It wasn't. This BYD brand's latest SUV can indeed retract its steering wheel right into the dashboard. However, it’s not quite used for the reason you’d think.

The Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range. BYD’s Chinese-market brand and naming structure can be confusing, but in essence, Fangchengbao is one of BYD's premium brands.

Power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving. The Tai 9 has a 66.5 kWh battery that is capable of BYD’s flash charging technology. The brand claims it can sprint from 10% to 97% in nine minutes.

According to recent reports, those are all very compelling specs, but the most interesting part of the Tai 9 is the top-of-the-line Foldable Smart Cabin trim. Since the Tai 9 uses a steer-by-wire system, the steering wheel can fold up and stow itself in the dashboard. BYD says that takes about 10 seconds.

Sources indicate that however, this isn’t for any sort of autonomous driving. China’s autonomous driving rules are strict, and no automaker in the country has approval for commercially sold eyes-off, hands-off driver assist features. Instead, the folding steering wheel is primarily for comfort and space, specifically when the car is stationary. Photos of the feature in action show that stowing away the steering wheel makes extra room for a little table setup.

In a recent development, this isn’t entirely unprecedented. The new trend in China is for large SUVs to be third spaces where buyers can comfortably hang out, even when they aren't driving. The Tai 9’s Nappa leather, comfy seats, and second-row folding screen are meant to make it a calming, relaxing space to spend time. It's similar in concept to what we’ve seen on the Zeekr Mix and SkyNomad N90 Studio.

Still, despite the Tai 9’s folding steering wheel not being for self-driving, I wouldn’t be surprised if it does show up in cars for that reason someday, as manufacturers strive to make cars that can truly drive themselves.

A car with no steering wheel at all might feel risky and uncomfortable to some car buyers, especially if it's like Tesla’s Cybercab, which can’t be driven manually at all above low speeds. Yet, if there were a backup to take control, I could see that putting some minds at ease.

Sources indicate that the Fangchengbao Tai 9 is on sale in China for about $42,000. The top-of-the-line model with the foldable steering wheel is about $49,500.

#63720. MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
